props.title: Risk management — the rules that keep you in the game
items: Risk only 1–2% of capital on any single trade
Always use a stop-loss on leveraged or active positions
Diversify across sectors AND asset classes
Never mix investing capital with trading capital
Never borrow / use MTF leverage to chase returns

captions: Chapter ten, the final chapter — risk management,
and putting the whole course together.
Everything we've learned means nothing without this.
The first job of an investor is not to make money —
it is to not go broke.
Survival first.
Here are the survival rules —
the discipline the ninety-one percent ignored.
One —
risk only one to two percent of your total capital on any single trade.
Then even ten losses in a row cannot ruin you.
This one rule separates survivors from casualties.
Two —
always use a stop-loss on any leveraged or active position.
Decide, before you enter, where you are wrong and will exit.
No exceptions, especially in futures and options.
Three — diversify across sectors and across asset classes.
Equities, some debt, a little gold.
When one zigs, another zags.
Four —
never mix your investing capital with your trading capital.
Keep the long-term wealth pot completely separate from the money you actively trade.
Five — never borrow money, or use margin-trading leverage,
to chase returns.
Remember the ninety-one percent —
leverage is what turned their losses catastrophic.
Follow these five,
and you will still be standing when opportunity comes.
So which of all these tools is for you?
Match the instrument to yourself — honestly.
If you are a beginner or a long-term investor,
your toolkit is simple and powerful: an index SIP plus a few quality stocks,
aimed at long-term wealth, needing just a few hours a month.
Futures and options?
Not yet — you don't need them.
If you are experienced, you can add hedging —
using futures to protect your portfolio —
while your core stays invested for growth,
with weekly research.
Here F&O earns its place, in small size, mainly for protection.
Only the dedicated, near full-time trader —
with a tested method and iron discipline —
should run active options strategies and trade commodities.
And even then, only with strict risk rules.
There is no shame in the first column.
It quietly builds more wealth for more people than the third ever will.
Let's bring the entire course together, in one breath.
Start with the sector — top-down,
from macro to sector to the leaders within it.
Research properly: the three statements, the key ratios,
the moat, and always a fair price with a margin of safety.
Learn from methods and trustworthy channels — Varsity,
honest educators, seasoned fund managers — and never from tips.
For equity strategy,
an index SIP and a few quality names serve most people beautifully,
even though you now know them all.
Futures and options are powerful tools —
use them to hedge first,
and never forget that ninety-one percent of speculators lose.
In commodities, let gold be a five-to-ten-percent hedge,
and always respect the leverage.
And binding it all — the risk rules that keep you in the game.
Survival first, returns second.
You now have the complete map.
Learn deeply, risk little, and compound patiently.
That is how wealth is truly built.
This is educational content, not investment advice —
do your own research, and consult a SEBI-registered adviser.
Thank you for watching.
